query: Controlling for priority and category, which underlying causes explain longer resolution times?

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Categorizing the underlying failure type is exactly the causal axis the query needs; it lets the analyst group resolution times by root cause. Values track the short_description well (VPN/WiFi/DB -> connection_failure, email system down -> service_down). Some fine distinctions (service_down vs connection_failure) require judgment but are reasonable readings.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Identifies the impacted system, a distinct and useful grouping dimension for explaining resolution-time differences. Values are cleanly derivable from the descriptions (vpn_client, network_infrastructure, database_server, email_server) and are well grounded.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope/blast-radius is a genuinely useful explanatory axis for longer resolutions. Grounding is weaker: 'Cannot connect to database' -> single_user and 'VPN connection issue' -> remote_access are inferences not stated, and 'system_wide' being the modal value suggests confident scope assignments the terse text often does not support.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Recurrence is a plausibly relevant driver of long resolution times, so it has analytical value. However it is a bare boolean and its derivation is unclear from the samples; the short_description alone rarely states recurrence, so many 'false'/'true' assignments appear inferred without visible support.

per_column.name: resolution_ownership_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket was handed across agents vs self-resolved vs unassigned is a meaningful process factor for resolution duration. It is derivable in principle from assigned_to/closed_by/sys_updated_by fields, but those are not shown in the samples, and the 'self_resolved' vs 'cross_agent_resolved' split for otherwise similar rows is not verifiable from the provided evidence.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively supply strong new causal axes (failure type, affected component, scope, recurrence, ownership pattern) precisely aligned with a query about what drives longer resolution times while controlling for priority and category. Failure_mode and affected_component are both highly useful and well grounded in the short_description. Scope_indicator, recurrence_signal, and resolution_ownership_pattern remain analytically valuable but rely on inferences the shown source text does not always support, lowering groundedness.
